The zabar letters are printed on pictures of hands (fingers), in three groups for the gesture poem (TPI).
The zer letters are printed on pictures of hands (fingers), in three groups for the gesture poem (TPI).
The pesh letters are printed on pictures of hands (fingers), in three groups for the gesture poem (TPI).
A three-picture story of letters on a swing: (1) the swing holds اَ and مَ; (2) the letter م jumps off and lands below; (3) م, now without its own vowel, joins اَ to make اَمْ.
A four-picture swing story: (1) اَ and وَ sit on the swing with a second وَ below; (2)–(3) the first و loses its vowel and joins اَ as اَوْ, and (4) the two و become one و with a shadd: اَوَّ.

issues: In the second group the book prints "فِیْهِ" with a standing zer on the ha (as printed).

The second teaching point in the book lists the excepted letters as "ء ھ ع ح غ خ ل ی ا ر د", as printed. Standard tajweed treats ل and ر as idgham without ghunnah, and the throat letters as izhar.
